The `baseline-binding-reader` contract is also closed and never raises. It depends directly on `retro-box-activation`; new `squatch/baseline.py` exposes immutable `BaselineResolution(state, binds)` where `state` is exactly `ABSENT | NO_GO | GO | REVOKED`. `resolve_baseline(config, events, *, specs_dir)` selects the latest complete `signal` whose kind is `review_baseline`: no record is `ABSENT`; any latest verdict other than `GO` is `NO_GO`; a `GO` record is `GO` only when its recorded identity equals the current `Registry(config)` resolution for every recorded tier on both `review` and `author` and its recorded `spec_major` equals the major versions loaded from `specs_dir/review.md` and `specs_dir/author.md`; otherwise it is `REVOKED`. Only `GO` sets `binds=true`. Missing/empty routing, unresolved placeholders, unknown tiers, malformed identity/spec fields, unreadable specs, and a torn journal tail all resolve to the supervised side (`REVOKED` for a selected GO, otherwise the applicable `ABSENT`/`NO_GO`) without escaping. The ticket migrates the existing implementation instead of adding a second reader: it removes `policy.go_binds`, leaves `policy.starting_state` as the sole starting-state policy, and makes `squatch/author.py` the sole production caller of `resolve_baseline`; Author passes its current config, `Journal.read()` events, and `<repo>/specs`, then passes `resolution.binds` into `policy.starting_state`. Registry and spec-major identity therefore reach the reader explicitly, never through globals. Its fence is new `squatch/baseline.py`/`tests/test_baseline.py` plus existing `squatch/journal.py`, `squatch/config.py`, `squatch/policy.py`, `tests/test_policy.py`, `squatch/author.py`, `tests/test_author.py`, and `tests/test_retro_box.py`.

The `retro-doctor-cli` contract closes both Phase 5 operator verbs. `retro` is the manual, forced retrospective over the current window: it takes the existing single-writer lock, composes the same shared provider/cooldown payload, Driver, `specs/retro.md`, Git/Effects, Box, and `Retro.run("manual", forced=True)` path as the drain hook, and never creates a second model client or report writer. With no merge after the latest completed report it prints exactly `retro: no merge since the latest completed report` and exits 0 without a model call or write. On success it prints `retro: committed tickets/retro/<next-zero-padded-seq>.md` and exits 0. A selected run that returns no report because the window is suppressed or the governed call/commit fails prints `retro: no report committed; inspect status and the Suggestion Box` and exits 1; the existing Retro failure signal and deduplicated Box report remain the durable detail. Lock, config, Git, construction, and journal failures retain the CLI's refusal rendering and exit 2. `doctor` is the section 18 mechanical self-check only, never a retro-window/model view: new `squatch/doctor.py` returns a deterministic ordered report for exactly `venv`, `git`, `config`, `lock`, and `journal`. It verifies the running interpreter is the checkout's `.venv`, `git` resolves and answers through the process seam, config loads through the real schema, the advisory lock is either available or has a parseable live-holder record, and every active/rolled journal record is readable. It reads only the interpreter/environment, Git version, config, lock record/state, and journal; it performs no filesystem, journal, ticket, Box, Git-repository, provider, or model write. CLI rendering is exactly one `doctor: ok|failed` summary followed by one `PASS|FAIL <name>: <bounded detail>` line in that fixed order. All pass exits 0; any failed check exits 2 after rendering all five checks, with exceptions converted to bounded details and no traceback. `tests/test_doctor.py` proves those feature behaviors with injected seams; `tests/test_retro.py`, `tests/test_cli.py`, and `tests/test_verbs.py` prove manual retro success/no-merge/failure, lock/refusal behavior, parser registration, output, exit codes, and preservation. Seed Context/on-demand partitions and synthetic sizes are tested only in `tests/test_seeded_phase5_03.py`, never as doctor feature criteria. Because this corrective addition legitimately grows section 20, the historical render guards in `tests/test_seeded_phase3_core.py`, `tests/test_seeded_phase3_03.py`, `tests/test_seeded_phase3_06.py`, `tests/test_seeded_phase3_13.py`, and `tests/test_seeded_phase3_22.py` pin their authoring-time section-20 length before rendering, just as they already pin Context sizes; later plan growth never retroactively invalidates an admitted seed.
